is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles funestus, a malaria vector (Abstract, page 1).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study genotypes CYP6P9a, CYP6P9b, L119F-GSTe2, and structural variants SV4.3 kb and SV6.5 kb (Methods, page 4).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Figure 4 (page 8) provides genotype frequency data (RR, RS, SS) for the markers across nine districts.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from field sites in Tanzania (Methods, page 3).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an original empirical research study (Abstract, page 1).

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is provided for nine specific districts in Tanzania (Methods, page 3; Figure 1).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections were conducted from November 2021 to December 2022 (Methods, page 3).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes a new, large-scale survey of insecticide resistance in Tanzania.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data, including genotype frequencies and bioassay results, are presented in the main figures and text.

assessment.summary: This study conducted a large-scale survey of insecticide resistance in Anopheles funestus across nine districts in Tanzania. It combined phenotypic bioassays (pyrethroids, carbamates, organochlorines, organophosphates) with genotyping of metabolic resistance markers (CYP6P9a, CYP6P9b, L119F-GSTe2, and structural variants SV4.3 kb and SV6.5 kb). The study found widespread pyrethroid resistance, which was reversible by PBO, and identified distinct geographical patterns in resistance markers.
